Theme

School & learning

classic noun and adjective

a model author of the first rank

also classics, a classic author, classical author, classical writer, the classics

post-classical

Gell. 19.8.15
Traupman 275
M-O s.v. classic, classical

scrīptor classicus

a classic author

Gellius’s figure from the census: the classicī were citizens of the first class, so a classicus scrīptor is a first-class writer, set against a prōlētārius, one of the lowest. Elsewhere classicus means “of the fleet”, as classicī mīlitēs, marines (Liv. 21.61.2). In modern Latin it is also “classical”, of Greek and Roman antiquity (Vives; M-O).

Other words

  • auctor, auctōris m. — an author, a writer whose word carries weight

    noun, third declension · also used · classical · Cic. Att. 12.18: iī quōs nunc lēctitō auctōrēs (Lewis & Short)

    The writer of a work, and the authority one follows; the word for the authors one reads as models. First of all the originator or founder of anything (Lewis & Short).

Examples

  • id est classicus adsiduusque aliquis scrīptor, nōn prōlētārius

    that is, some classic writer of standing, not one of the rabbleGell. 19.8.15

See also classic, book, Latin.
